status: Project design requirement; NASA analogy reviewed; qualification open
requirement: The heat-shield forebody shall use a 70 degree cone half-angle from the symmetry axis, equivalent to 20 degrees from the shield reference plane, consistent with NASA Mars sphere-cone examples. Backshell geometry shall be sized independently.
assumption: Backshell height/diameter = 0.75 retains the Rev09 0.6 m packaging height as a provisional backshell allocation. Forebody cone envelope (D/2)tan20° is added; spherical nose and shoulder blends, cover crown and actual internal volume require CAD. This is a packaging assumption, not NASA dimensions.
nasaRationale: NASA Pathfinder and MSL use a 70 degree half-angle sphere-cone forebody. Adopt this angle convention for FREYA. NASA heritage does not prescribe FREYA backshell slope, nose radius, height, stability or TPS.

sources.title: NASA PDS: Mars Pathfinder Lander Description
NASA: Aerodynamic Challenges for the Mars Science Laboratory Entry, Descent and Landing
NASA: Aeroshell for Mars Science Laboratory

verification: Analytical geometry test across supported diameters; later CAD inspection, packaging clearance review and aerodynamic/thermal qualification required. NASA heritage does not verify FREYA performance.
